name: AnyPS5
description: Tool for automatic PS5 executables porting to Linux and Windows
one_liner: A tool that takes PlayStation 5 games and converts them so they can run directly on a regular PC, without emulating the console.
buyer: Honestly, nobody paying. This is a hobbyist/enthusiast project aimed at PC gamers and reverse-engineering hobbyists, and it sits in a legal gray area around game publishers' rights.
business_use_cases: A hobbyist community builds compatibility lists and shares ported games for free, similar to existing console emulation scenes.
An engine-porting specialist studies the relinker approach to build client work porting other consoles' titles, not this project itself.
A hardware reviewer uses performance data from it to benchmark PC builds against console performance.

money_ideas.idea: None viable directly — distributing or monetizing ported copyrighted games invites takedowns and legal risk.

steal_this: Nothing to responsibly ship this weekend — the only 'product' here is porting copyrighted game binaries, which is a legal liability, not a business.
